# MCCPS — Merchant Credit Card Processing Services

> US merchant services company: credit/debit card processing in store, online, by phone and mobile via the PayPilot by MCCPS platform; free statement analysis; Zero Processing Fees (compliant dual pricing) program; next-day funding; PCI help; 24/7 support at 844.826.6227. Independent sales agent program.

## Blog
- [How Credit Card Processing Works, Step by Step](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/how-credit-card-processing-works/): Follow a card payment from tap to deposit: authorization, clearing, settlement, and the parties that touch every sale. A plain-English guide for merchants.
- [Interchange Fees Explained](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/interchange-explained/): Interchange is the largest part of card processing cost. Learn who sets it, why it varies by card and sale type, and what you can and cannot control.
- [Card Network Assessment Fees Explained](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/assessment-fees-explained/): Assessment fees are the small card network charges stacked on every sale. See what they cover, how they are calculated, and where they show up on statements.
- [Processor Markup: What You're Really Paying For](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/processor-markup-explained/): Processor markup is the one part of your card fees that is actually negotiable. Learn how it is built, how to spot it, and what to ask before you sign.
- [Your Effective Rate: The Only Number That Matters](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/effective-rate-explained/): Your effective rate is total processing fees divided by card volume. Learn how to calculate it, what a typical range looks like, and how to lower it.
- [Tiered Pricing: Qualified vs. Non-Qualified](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/tiered-pricing-explained/): Tiered pricing sorts card sales into qualified, mid-qualified and non-qualified buckets. See how it works, why it hides costs, and what to ask instead.
- [Flat-Rate vs. Interchange-Plus Pricing](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/flat-rate-vs-interchange-plus/): Flat-rate is simple and interchange-plus is transparent. Compare the two pricing models with worked math, and learn which fits your volume and ticket size.
- [Subscription (Membership) Pricing for Processing](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/membership-and-subscription-pricing/): Membership or subscription pricing charges a monthly fee and passes interchange through at a thin markup. See how it works and who it fits best.
- [Dual Pricing Explained](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/dual-pricing-explained/): Dual pricing lists a cash price and a card price. Learn how it works, how it differs from surcharging, and the disclosure rules to confirm before you start.
- [Cash Discount vs. Surcharge: What's the Difference?](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/cash-discount-vs-surcharge/): Cash discounts and surcharges both offset card fees but follow different rules. Compare how each works, what disclosure is expected, and what to verify.
- [Credit Card Surcharge Rules: What to Check in Your State](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/surcharge-rules-by-state/): Surcharge rules differ by state and card network and change often. Here is a practical checklist of what to verify before adding a credit card surcharge.
- [Convenience Fees Explained](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/convenience-fees-explained/): A convenience fee is not the same as a surcharge. Learn what card networks expect, when a convenience fee applies, and what to verify before charging one.
- [Debit vs. Credit: Why Costs Differ](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/debit-vs-credit-processing-costs/): Debit and credit cards can cost a merchant very different amounts. See why regulated debit is cheaper, how rewards credit changes things, and what it means.
- [Why Rewards Cards Cost Merchants More](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/rewards-cards-cost-more/): Rewards and premium credit cards carry higher interchange. Learn how points and cash back are funded, what it costs you, and how to manage the impact.
- [Card-Present vs. Card-Not-Present Transactions](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/card-present-vs-card-not-present/): Card-present and card-not-present sales differ in cost, fraud risk and chargeback liability. Learn what each means and how to protect your business.
- [What Is a Merchant Account?](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/what-is-a-merchant-account/): A merchant account is the business account that lets you accept card payments and receive settlement. Learn how it works, what it costs and how to get one.
- [Payment Facilitator vs. Dedicated Merchant Account](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/payment-facilitator-vs-merchant-account/): A payment facilitator pools merchants under one account; a dedicated merchant account is yours alone. Compare cost, speed, holds, and control side by side.
- [What Is an ISO in Payments?](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/what-is-an-iso/): An ISO, or independent sales organization, sells and supports card processing on behalf of banks. See what ISOs do, how they earn, and how agents fit in.
- [What Is a Payment Gateway?](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/what-is-a-payment-gateway/): A payment gateway securely carries card data from your checkout or terminal to the processor. Learn what it does, what it costs, and when you need one.
- [Payment Processor vs. Payment Gateway](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/payment-processor-vs-gateway/): Processors and gateways are often confused. See what each does, how they work together, and why knowing the difference helps you avoid paying twice.
- [How to Read a Merchant Statement](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/how-to-read-a-merchant-statement/): A merchant statement hides your true cost in dense tables. Learn each section, which numbers to pull, and how to calculate your effective rate in minutes.
- [12 Hidden Fees on Merchant Statements](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/hidden-fees-on-merchant-statements/): Twelve fees that commonly hide in merchant statements, what each is, when it is legitimate, and the question to ask your processor about it.
- [The PCI Non-Compliance Fee and How to Stop Paying It](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/pci-non-compliance-fee/): A PCI non-compliance fee shows up when your annual validation is incomplete. Learn what triggers it, how to choose the right SAQ, and how to end the charge.
- [Processor Early Termination Fees](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/early-termination-fees/): Early termination fees can make leaving a card processor expensive. Learn how ETFs, liquidated damages and auto-renewals work and how to read your contract.
- [Leasing vs. Buying a Card Terminal](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/terminal-leasing-vs-buying/): Should you lease or buy a credit card terminal? Compare total cost over time, contract risks, upgrade options and when reusing your own terminal wins.
- [POS Features That Matter for Small Businesses](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/best-pos-features-small-business/): A practical checklist of point-of-sale features small businesses need, from inventory and reporting to offline mode, integrations and payment flexibility.
- [The EMV Liability Shift Explained](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/emv-liability-shift/): The EMV liability shift moved counterfeit card fraud costs to the party with the weaker technology. Learn how it works and what it means for your business.
- [Contactless Payments: A Merchant Guide](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/contactless-payments-guide/): How contactless NFC payments work, what you need to accept tap cards and phones, how limits and security behave, and how it affects speed and cost.
- [Apple Pay, Google Pay & Mobile Wallets Explained](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/mobile-wallets-explained/): How mobile wallets like Apple Pay and Google Pay use tokenization, what they mean for fraud and fees, and how to accept them in store and online.
- [Payment Tokenization Explained](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/tokenization-explained/): Payment tokenization replaces card numbers with safe stand-ins. Learn how tokens work, how they reduce PCI scope, and where they fit in your setup.
- [Point-to-Point Encryption (P2PE) Explained](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/encryption-p2pe-explained/): P2PE encrypts card data at the terminal so your systems never see it. Learn how it works, how it differs from tokenization, and how it affects PCI.
- [3-D Secure Explained](https://mccps.fastapi.online/blog/3d-secure-explained/): 3-D Secure adds an authentication step to online card payments and can shift fraud liability. Learn how 3DS 2 works, its tradeoffs, and when to use it.
